Gojo · opt-in experiment

Protect a new idea, then make it pay its way.

8 seeds · 81,920 physical world requests · five fixed controllers

The paired admission effect was small and inconclusive: +0.007 net resource per request versus unconditional replacement (95% interval [-0.005, 0.019]). Existing error had the highest mean whole-group return. Their aggregate physical gross was equal; the net difference came from paid burn. Individual decisions and seed returns can still differ.

Startup funds are finite. Later candidate work uses service-earned fees. Those fees move existing resource between structures; physical gross minus paid burn tells whether the group gains resource. Prices are abstract.

Where the work went

Train 16 · validate 32 · seed cap 320 · known ≥24 · retry ≥64 purchases. Paired admission requires a positive resource gain after all trial work and the known-coverage threshold. The unfiltered control pays for the same block but promotes every completed candidate. Unknown is open, not zero; an open candidate uses the incumbent decision for its projected consequence.

Pending trials were still training or validating when the run ended. “Low coverage” includes completed blocks with fewer than 24 known candidate reads. Aborted blocks are incomplete; that alone does not establish a funding cause. Legacy controllers have no candidate-trial records.

Noise is source 2 throughout. Source 3's earlier noise and later useful phase are kept separate in analysis. First16 figures use world requests, so unserved demand remains visible. Grants are paid base-gate permissions, including during validation freezes; they are not counts of successful ordinal updates. Per-source burn is allocated by request, not counterfactual causal credit.

What this can establish

The test evaluates a supplied candidate grammar and a fixed native funding/admission law. Favorable selection on a small block can still be luck. Fresh physical results and independent-noise trials are needed to check that.

Audit scope and interpretation limits
  • All-task endpoint includes holds, startup, failed work and rejected trials.
  • Only eight independent seed differences receive descriptive unadjusted t(7) intervals; two-seed pilots have none.
  • Fees redistribute conserved funds; actual physical gross minus real burn defines group return.
  • Costs are abstract. Candidate replay estimates cannot mint external income.
  • Both structures are frozen during the declared shared validation block; candidate open reuses the incumbent projected resource and contributes exactly zero paired gain.
  • Phase and source quality are evaluator labels, never learner inputs.
  • Burn is assigned to its world request; per-source net is not causal contribution credit.
  • Fresh16 windows are descriptive, stop before another promotion and may include online learning after each prediction.
  • Reported row updates count base-predictor updates only. Candidate trainingCount counts paid physical training experiences, not successful ordinal updates.
  • A promoted candidate can later learn as the current model. Historical trial roots retain live model carrier state; captured validation publications preserve what was evaluated, not a permanent frozen model snapshot.
  • Supplier reserve is its last observed request-time balance, not a simultaneous final balance across all services.
  • Post-first-closure windows begin at different times and are selection-conditioned; fixed final-phase results are also reported.
  • A fee-funded service can remain solvent while the whole system loses physical resource.
  • Trial causes inferred from coverage/gain are diagnostics; an incomplete trial alone does not identify why it aborted.
  • Saved archive checks cover their declared retained-anchor and paid-gate fixture, not a whole-world restart.

Offline review. All data are embedded; this page performs no simulation, network requests or paid model calls. Earlier review pages and modes remain available.
